326025.title: Weight-four size-one non-root class enumeration conjecture
326025.review_depth: Source arXiv:1307.8216v2 (final version; Contemp. Math. 633) Sections 1, 2, 5 and Appendix headers read. Authors' data page fetched; data files 404 (receipts kept).
326025.disposition: Independent implementation (scripts/f2classes.py): direct Whitehead minimality via all 8 one-letter automorphisms, J-canonical forms (rotations x 8 permutations), size 1 iff every level one-letter image stays in the J-class (valid because Gamma(W) is connected by Whitehead's theorem), root words by the Theorem 1.6 equality case (both bar readings agree with direct minimality on all cyclically reduced words of length <= 8). Validated against the source's own weight-2 (n=5..16) and weight-3 (n=7..20) formulas. Weight-4 counts agree with the conjectured quasi-polynomial for EVERY n = 9..27 (source data only reached n = 20). No counterexample; a full proof would require a literal Lean model of Aut(F2), minimal words and Whitehead peak reduction (not in mathlib or Lean Pool, whose WhiteheadTheorem is the topological one). Parked.
326025.computation: logs/f2-validate.log, logs/f2-wt2.log, logs/f2-wt3.log, logs/f2-wt4-9-28.log (n=28 not reached inside the 100 s cap)

372424.title: The two-thirds conjecture for the total isolation number
372424.review_depth: Source arXiv:2601.03363v1 (only version) Sections 1-3 and 5 read, including the rule, Observation 1 (P5), Theorems 1-5 and the sharpness family. Unindexed prior exposure: lanes/sol-fresh-source-discovery-r131 (288 random graphs, five path unions; parked, no exclusion) retained.
372424.disposition: Exact minimax solver (scripts/isogame.py) reproduces the source values (P5: D=2, S=4; P3, C3: 2; P6, C6: 4). Exhaustive census: ALL graphs of order <= 9 whose components have order >= 3 (12189 of order <= 8; 261434 of order 9 = 261080 connected + 354 disconnected, matching OEIS counts): no violation; equality 3D = 2n occurs only at n = 3, 6, 9 (2, 5, 10 graphs). Only two connected graphs of order <= 9 (both of order 5: P5 and one other) have Staller-start value above 2n/3; all 50 disjoint unions of these with P3, C3, P4, P6, C6 up to order 15 satisfy the bound. All free trees of order <= 14 (5421 trees of order 10..14): no violation (max D-values 6, 6, 7, 8, 8 for n = 10..14). No proof route beyond r131's identified charging gap.

372565.title: Directional dichotomy conjecture for sets of size p in finite affine 3-space
372565.review_depth: Source arXiv:2601.09910v1 Section 7 read; the conjecture is Mattheus's 2022 PhD thesis Conjecture 6.2.7 (thesis body not obtained).
372565.disposition: Exhaustive (scripts/directions.py, AGL(3,p)-normalised so that A contains 0, e1, e2, e3): p = 5 (121 sets): minimum 8 directions; p = 7 (6435689 sets): minimum 9 = p + 2 directions (e.g. {0, +-e1, +-e2, +-e3}). So both the p + 1 and the p + 2 forms hold for p = 5, 7 (p = 3 is vacuous). Simple structured families (three parallel lines; two skew lines) give at least 2p - 2 directions by Cauchy-Davenport. p = 11 is out of exhaustive reach. Parked.

373480.title: Odd-cycle two-line trade conjecture for Latin squares
373480.review_depth: Source arXiv:2603.06692v1 Section 4 (Experiments 1-3, Definitions 2-3, Lemmas 2-3, Conjectures 6-7, Table 2) read.
373480.disposition: The literal Conjecture 7 is false for trivial reasons: a matching permutation of two lines of a Latin square has no fixed points, so for n = 2 and n = 4 it never has an odd cycle (all 4 reduced squares of order 4 fail, checked); for n = 2^k every Cayley table of a 2-group fails (translation cycles have 2-power length), e.g. Z_2^3 at n = 8, inside the author's tested range, where the author already lists 'genuine absence of an odd-cycle trade' as a possible cause of the n = 8 success-rate dip (Table 2: 0.85). These are smallest-order/classical-group defects (zero credit). Exhaustive check: every one of the 9408 reduced Latin squares of order 6 has an odd-cycle trade in some view.

373706.title: Four-parts conjecture for biregular bipartite labeled multigraphs
373706.review_depth: Source arXiv:2603.18253v1 (only version) read in full (Conjectures 1-5, Theorems 1-8, proofs).
373706.disposition: Exact reformulation (scripts/fourparts.py): psi exists iff the k1 x n2 grid R1 x L2 admits fillings alpha (row-b multiplicities A[.][b]) and delta (column-c multiplicities B[c][.]) with (alpha, delta) a bijection onto L1 x R2. Theorem 3 plus the two symmetries (swap of the two graphs; simultaneous transpose) cover r = k1/n1 or 1/r integral and n1 = n2 with small epsilon. Exhaustive over all orbit classes: (2,3,4,6): 4 x 8 = 32 pairs; (2,3,6,9): 6 x 31 = 186 pairs; all feasible. Sampled (configuration model and vertex-like extreme matrices): (3,4,6,8) 300, (7,10,7,10) 100 random + 300 extreme, (4,6,6,9) 2000 extreme: all feasible, MRV search at most 154 nodes. No counterexample; general proof not found.

373718.title: Conjecture on the 2-tone chromatic number of cubic Halin graphs
373718.review_depth: Source arXiv:2603.18674v1 (only version) Sections 1 and 3 (Definition 1.1, Conjecture 1.1, Theorem 3.1 proof, Conjecture 3.1) read.
373718.disposition: Cubic Halin graphs with l leaves correspond to triangulations of the convex l-gon (dual tree); n = 2l - 2. Exhaustive backtracking (scripts/halin2tone.py; triangle labels fixed to 01|23|45 by S6 symmetry; every colouring re-verified): every cubic Halin graph of order 6..28 is 2-tone 6-colourable (l = 4..15; Catalan(13) = 742900 triangulations at l = 15). Controls: K = 5 fails on all (triangles). A naive induction (contract the deepest triangle) is NOT reducible: 73968 of 120000 generic boundary colourings admit no extension without recolouring (scripts/halinreduce.py), so a proof needs recolouring or a global construction. Conjecture very likely true; no proof; a literal Lean endpoint would also need a combinatorial model of plane Halin graphs. Parked as the strongest finite lead.
